title: Miracles confirm Law and Gospel; God would not lend omnipotence to a lying claim
pass_a_gloss: Besides, the-doctrine in the-Scriptures handed-down, and-so Scripture, which the-foundation of-it is, divine to-be and from God to-have-flowed, is-proved from the-miracles which in of-that-doctrine confirmation done were. Since indeed of-Scripture and of-heavenly doctrine two are chief parts, Law, and Gospel: the-law indeed confirmed was by-those wonders which in the-desert happened: as that the-living voice of-God speaking from midst of-fire heard was, that forty years in the-desert manna rained, that water often from the-rock led-out was, and-that of-the-Israelites the-clothes in-that whole time worn-out not were, and more of-that-kind. To-the-Gospel truly testimony bore almost infinite of-Christ miracles: then those visible and plainly stupendous of-the-Holy Spirit gifts, which poured-out were upon the-first believers: so that suddenly with-various and foreign tongues they-spoke, diseases any they-healed, demons they-expelled, and wonders other very-many they-performed. Since indeed such-things are above of-nature powers, necessary it-is God in them to-have-exercised his power. But unholy it-is to-think God to-have-willed to-use his omnipotence toward faith to-be-made for-Scripture and doctrine, which falsely and by-injury to-him was-ascribed, as-if he-had-willed by compact with men to-lie.
pass_b_english: Besides, that the doctrine handed down in the Scriptures — and so Scripture, which is its foundation — is divine and flowed from God is proved from the miracles done in confirmation of that doctrine. For since Scripture and heavenly doctrine have two chief parts, Law and Gospel: the law was confirmed by those wonders that happened in the desert — that the living voice of God speaking was heard from the midst of fire, that for forty years manna rained in the desert, that water was often led out from the rock, and that the Israelites' clothes were not worn out in that whole time, and more of that kind. To the Gospel almost infinite miracles of Christ bore witness; then those visible and plainly stupendous gifts of the Holy Spirit poured out on the first believers, so that suddenly they spoke in various and foreign tongues, healed any diseases, expelled demons, and performed very many other wonders. Since such things are above nature's powers, it is necessary that God exercised his power in them. But it is unholy to think God willed to use his omnipotence to make faith for a Scripture and doctrine falsely and injuriously ascribed to him, as if he had willed by compact with men to lie.
source_text: XVI. Praeterea doctrinam in Scripturis traditam, adeoque Scripturam, quae fundamentum illius est, divinam esse et a Deo manasse, probatur ex miraculis quae in doctrinae istius confirmationem facta sunt. Cum enim Scripturae et doctrinae caelestis duae sint praecipuae partes, Lex, et Evangelium: lex quidem confirmata est mirabilibus illis quae in deserto contigerunt: ut quod viva vox Dei loquentis e medio ignis audita est, quod quadraginta annis in deserto manna pluit, quod aqua saepius e petra educta est, quodque Israelitarum vestes toto illo tempore attritae non fuerunt, et plura ejusmodi. Evangelio vero testimonium perhibuerunt infinita pene Christi miracula: tum visibilia illa et plane stupenda Spiritus sancti dona, quae effusa sunt in primos credentes: ita ut subito variis et peregrinis linguis loquerentur, morbos quosvis sanarent, daemones expellerent, et miranda alia quam plurima patrarent. Cum enim talia sint supra naturae vires, necesse est Deum in illis exeruisse suam potentiam. At nefas est cogitare Deum voluisse uti sua omnipotentia ad fidem faciendam Scripturae et doctrinae, quae falso et injuria ipsi ascribebatur, quasi voluisset ex pacto cum hominibus mentiri.
